flight.hint.0.0: Something in the seat pocket is not the usual magazine.
flight.hint.0.1: Turn to the seat in front of Mary and look at the pocket.
flight.hint.0.2: Tap the folded note poking out of the seat pocket.
flight.hint.1.0: The screen in front of Mary is asleep. What does it want?
flight.hint.1.1: Tap the dark screen: it asks for the London time when we land. The flight card in the seat pocket knows when we land.
flight.hint.1.2: Tap the seat pocket and take the flight card: landing at 13:40, Singapore time.
flight.hint.2.0: 13:40 is Singapore time. London is behind Singapore. How far behind?
flight.hint.2.1: The crew keep two clocks in the galley at the back, one for each city.
flight.hint.2.2: Go through the curtain at the back and tap the two clocks: Singapore 12:40, London 05:40. Seven hours apart.
flight.hint.3.0: Landing at 13:40 in Singapore. Take seven hours off for London.
flight.hint.3.1: Tap the dark seat-back screen and turn the hours down, seven times.
flight.hint.3.2: Set the screen to 06:40 and tap Wake.
flight.hint.4.0: The note is written backwards. What turns writing the right way round?
flight.hint.4.1: A mirror does. The dark seat-back screen is as shiny as one, and the toilet at the back has a real mirror over its basin.
flight.hint.4.2: Hold the backwards note (tap it in the strip), then tap the dark seat-back screen; or open the toilet door in the galley and tap the mirror with the note.
flight.hint.5.0: The magazine in the seat pocket is worth a look.
flight.hint.5.1: Tap the magazine in the seat pocket, then tap it in the strip to open it.
flight.hint.5.2: Open the magazine: the Junior Explorer page says to ask the crew for a magnifying glass.
flight.hint.6.0: The magazine says to ask the crew for the magnifying glass.
flight.hint.6.1: Priya is in the galley behind the curtain, with the breakfast trays.
flight.hint.6.2: Tap Priya in the galley and she will give you the magnifying glass.
flight.hint.7.0: The magazine says to ask the crew for the magnifying glass.
flight.hint.7.1: Priya has left the galley: breakfast is coming up the aisle.
flight.hint.7.2: Turn to the back of the cabin and tap Priya at the trolley; she will give you the magnifying glass.
flight.hint.8.0: The map is awake, and the note says: find the moth.
flight.hint.8.1: The moth is too small to see. A magnifying glass makes small things big.
flight.hint.8.2: Tap the magnifying glass in the strip, then tap the map on the screen.
flight.hint.9.0: Someone has doodled on the map. The note says which drawing matters.
flight.hint.9.1: Find the moth among the drawings, near the top of London.
flight.hint.9.2: Tap the little moth beside Enfield.
flight.note.flightcard: Flight information Landing: 13:40 Singapore time Flight time: 14 hours. Breakfast is served one hour before landing. Please keep your seat belt fastened while seated.
flight.note.noteMirror: It’s all backwards. Every letter the wrong way round. Mary can’t read a word of it.
flight.note.noteRead: The note, in the mirror Look at the map. Find the moth. It knows the way. – N
flight.card: Elliot and Zaina are asleep across the aisle. Mary is not. The cabin is dark and quiet, and something in the seat pocket in front of her is not the usual magazine.
flight.meanwhile: Meanwhile, somewhere over Europe, Mary is the only one awake in row 34.
flight.comic.0.0: Night at the airport. Suitcases on the pavement, one with a jar of kaya in it.
flight.comic.2.0: And in the seat pocket, beside the magazine…
flight.comic.2.1: something that was not the usual magazine.
flight.intro: Hour thirteen of fourteen. Dawn at the window, and everyone asleep but you. Something in the seat pocket in front of you is not the usual magazine.
flight.postcard: Wheels down! Fourteen hours and I did not sleep a wink. Somebody left a backwards note in my seat pocket, so I read it in the dark screen like a mirror: look at the map, find the moth. I woke the screen with London time (06:40, seven hours behind Singapore, the galley clocks told me), borrowed a magnifying glass from Priya, and there it was: a tiny moth drawn right beside Enfield. Elliot and Zaina slept through all of it.

nana.hint.0.1: The attic is above the landing, up the stairs.
nana.hint.0.2: Go up the stairs and look at the hatch in the landing ceiling.

nana.hint.2.1: Nana might make an exception if you brought her something. Your suitcase is upstairs in the spare room.
nana.hint.2.2: Take Nana’s present out of your suitcase and give it to her in the kitchen.

nana.hint.5.0: A tin hidden by a nine-year-old has a code a nine-year-old would choose.
nana.hint.5.1: The photographs going up the stairs have dates on their plates.
nana.hint.5.2: Tap the photographs on the stair wall and read every plate.
nana.hint.6.0: The tin is in the attic.
nana.hint.6.1: Once you are up and can see, look on the shelf.
nana.hint.6.2: Tap the old tin on the shelf in the attic.
nana.hint.7.0: Nana was nine when she hid the tin. Which year was she nine?

nana.hint.7.2: Set the tin’s dials to 1, 9, 6, 7 and tap Open.

nana.hint.8.1: The torch is in your suitcase, in the spare room upstairs.
nana.hint.8.2: Tap the spare room door on the landing, then take the torch from the suitcase.
nana.hint.9.2: Tap the torch in the strip, then tap the dark.
nana.hint.10.0: The tin is open. Nana’s map is inside.
nana.hint.10.1: Tap the map to take it.
nana.hint.10.2: Take the folded map from the tin.
nana.hint.11.2: Tap the map in the strip, then Nana.
nana.card: Nana and Jedi’s house, with the last of the sun on the front door. Elliot and Zaina are asleep on the sofa. Nana is making tea, Jedi is resting his eyes, and Nana has said one thing to Mary: “There is something of mine in the attic, from when I was nine. If you can get up there.”
nana.meanwhile: Meanwhile, in Enfield, Mary has been sent up to the attic for something of Nana’s.
nana.comic.0.0: Nana at the barrier, waving with both arms.
nana.comic.0.1: Jedi said he had carried all the bags.
nana.comic.1.0: The end of the road, the end of the day.
nana.comic.1.1: The last of the sun on Nana’s front door.
nana.comic.2.0: “There is something of mine in the attic,” said Nana.
nana.comic.2.1: “From when I was nine. If you can get up there.”
nana.intro: Enfield, the first evening. Tea in a minute, Jedi resting his eyes, and something of Nana’s in the attic, if you can get up there.
nana.postcard: Enfield at last! Nana sent me up to the attic for a tin she hid when she was nine. Jedi charged me a biscuit for the loft pole, the attic was pitch dark (the torch, Nana was right), and the code was the year she was nine: 1967, from the photos on the stairs. Inside was a map she drew of Trent Park, with a little house in the trees that is not on any real map. I showed her. She just smiled and said: well, go on then.
park.hint.0.0: Nana said the little house is past the obelisk, in the trees by the moat, and only shows itself at dusk to someone who is looking.
park.hint.0.1: Nana is at the café table. Her map is in the strip.
park.hint.0.2: Tap Nana at the café, and open the map in the strip.
park.hint.1.0: People once listened very carefully in the big house. Something there is still sending.
park.hint.1.1: On the terrace of the big house a little brass lamp keeps flashing, beside a brass mouthpiece in the wall.
park.hint.1.2: Go up to the terrace, turn to the urn, and tap the little lamp. Count the flashes.
park.hint.2.0: The flashes come in pairs of numbers. Numbers in pairs want a grid.
park.hint.2.1: The museum in the basement keeps the listeners’ code card on the wall.
park.hint.2.2: Through the museum door, turn to the display cabinet and tap the framed card.
park.hint.3.0: The lamp is sending a word: one, five; one, one; four, two. The card turns each pair into a letter.
park.hint.3.1: Row one, column five is E. Row one, column one is A. Row four, column two is R. The listeners’ box opens on the word it is sent.
park.hint.3.2: At the box, tap once, pause, tap five times, pause, tap once, pause, tap once, pause, tap four times, pause, tap twice. Then Open.
park.hint.4.1: Among the replicas is a folded paper that is not one.
park.hint.4.2: Take the folded paper from the box and read it.
park.hint.5.0: Nana drew her map when she was nine. She marked something on it.
park.hint.5.1: Open the map in the strip and look near the obelisk.
park.hint.5.2: There is a cross by the obelisk, where its shadow points, and a line about digging at dusk.
park.hint.6.0: Digging needs something to dig with.
park.hint.6.1: Zaina brought her spade from the sandpit. It is on the grass by her chair at the café.
park.hint.6.2: Tap the little red spade on the grass by Zaina’s chair.
park.hint.7.0: Where does the obelisk’s shadow point?
park.hint.7.1: The shadow lies across the grass towards the old tree at the wood’s edge, east of the obelisk, with a hollow in its roots.
park.hint.7.2: Tap the spade in the strip, then the hollow among the old tree’s roots.
park.hint.8.2: Tap the key in the hole.
park.hint.9.0: Nana said back by dark. Nobody knows what time it is.
park.hint.9.1: Jedi’s watch has stopped. He is on the bench on the lawn, resting his eyes.
park.hint.10.0: A stopped watch needs a clock. The park has an old one.
park.hint.10.1: The obelisk is a sundial: Nana’s ring of stones has the hours painted on it, and the shadow is the hand.
park.hint.10.2: Go to the obelisk and look at the shadow and the stones.
park.hint.11.0: The shadow lies between the stones marked VII and VIII.
park.hint.11.1: That is about twenty to eight. Open the watch in the strip.
park.hint.11.2: Set the watch to seven forty and tap Set.
park.hint.12.0: The paper said: through the little gate in the old wall, past the moat.
park.hint.12.1: The gate is in the old wall in the wood beyond the moat, and it is locked.
park.hint.12.2: Tap the rusty key in the strip, then the gate.
park.hint.13.0: The paper said: at dusk, to someone who is looking.
park.hint.13.1: It is not dusk until Mary knows how late it is: Jedi’s watch, set by the sundial.
park.hint.13.2: Set the watch to twenty to eight; then open the gate and look.
park.hint.14.2: Tap the little house in the trees.
park.note.card: The listeners’ tap code. Tap the row, pause, tap the column. Two taps, a pause, three taps is H. C and K share a square.
park.note.history: THIS HOUSE IN THE WAR From 1942 to 1945 the most important prisoners of the war were kept in this house, and treated like guests. They did not know that the house was listening: down here, people with headphones on wrote down everything the prisoners said, through tiny microphones hidden in the lamps, the plant pots, even the garden benches. Most of the listeners had themselves escaped from Germany and Austria. What they heard helped to end the war sooner. The house is a museum now.
park.note.paper: If you are reading this, you listened, like the men downstairs did. There is a house in the trees past the moat that is not on any map. It shows itself at dusk, to someone who is looking, through the little gate in the old wall. I buried the key where the obelisk’s shadow points when the moths come out. If you’re reading this, bring them home. N., age 9
park.card: Nana’s map, and a whole golden evening. Nana, Jedi, Elliot and Zaina at the café on the lawn, and Nana has said: “The little house is past the obelisk, in the trees by the moat. It only shows itself at dusk, to someone who is looking. Back by dark.”
park.meanwhile: Meanwhile, in Trent Park, Mary is following Nana’s map towards the trees.
park.comic.0.0: Jedi parked by the gates, mostly on the grass.
park.comic.0.1: Mary had the map. Zaina had the spade.
park.comic.1.0: “Past the obelisk, in the trees by the moat,” said Nana.
park.comic.1.1: “It only shows itself at dusk, to someone who is looking.”
park.comic.2.0: The avenue went on for ever, and the moth went first.
park.intro: Trent Park, the next evening. Nana’s map in the strip, the family at the café, and the little house past the obelisk, if it shows itself.
park.postcard: Trent Park, at dusk! Nana’s map had a cross by the obelisk, and a lamp in the big house was flashing a word in the listeners’ tap code: EAR. The box it opened had a note in it from a girl called N., age nine, and I dug up her key where the obelisk’s shadow points. Jedi’s watch had stopped, so I read the time off the sundial (twenty to eight) and while I was looking down the whole park turned blue. Then, through a little gate in an old wall in the wood: a house. With moths. Nana just said: go on, then. So I am going.

eschool.hint.6.2: Tap the run, then Roll. The marble does the rest.

eschool.note.card: On the front, in Miss Okafor’s writing: Goodbye, Elliot! Open me after the marble run works. And not without your jumper! Love from everyone in 2P
eschool.note.cardOpen: Inside the card, twenty-nine names, and: Have the best summer, Elliot. Keep asking how things work. Miss O x And in the corner, in someone’s pencil: a little moth.
eschool.card: Classroom 2P, with balloons on the whiteboard and a party waiting. Miss Okafor has left Elliot a card on her desk, and the marble run on the wall has never once rung its bell.
eschool.meanwhile: Meanwhile, in Classroom 2P, Elliot has a marble run to mend before anyone touches the cake.
eschool.comic.0.0: Balloons on the whiteboard. Cake on the table.
eschool.comic.1.0: The marble run on the wall had never once rung its bell.
eschool.comic.2.0: On Miss Okafor’s desk, a card with his name on it.
eschool.comic.3.0: Somewhere out there was his jumper.
eschool.comic.3.1: Nobody goes home without their jumper.
eschool.intro: Last day of term. Balloons on the whiteboard, cake on the table, and a card with your name on it on Miss Okafor’s desk.
eschool.postcard: The marble run was missing three pieces: one in the tray, one in the sandpit and one under the jumpers in lost property. The chalk wall showed where they went, and when I pressed Roll the marble went ALL the way and rang the bell. I found my jumper too (rocket badge). Miss Okafor’s card has everybody’s name in it and someone drew a moth. See you at the airport!

howto: Tap anything you are curious about. The little arrows turn you round. Things you pick up wait in the strip: tap one, then tap where it goes. And if you are stuck, tap me.
tip.tap: Tap anything you are curious about. The little arrows at the sides turn you round.
tip.pickup: Things you pick up wait in the strip below. Tap one to hold it, then tap where it belongs.
tip.hold: Now tap the thing it goes with. Tap it in the strip again to put it down.
tip.combine: Two things in the strip can go together: hold one, then tap the other.
tip.help: If you get stuck, tap me at the top: your notebook has a hint for every riddle. And hold a finger on the room to see everything you can tap.
tip.helpPoint: If you get stuck, tap me at the top and I’ll fly to the next thing to look at.
